new_scholarship.name: ACIAR Pacific Agriculture Scholarships and Support Program (PASS)
new_scholarship.official_source: Australian Centre for International Agricultural Research (ACIAR)
new_scholarship.description: The Pacific Agriculture Scholarships and Support (PASS) Program funds postgraduate research scholarships in agriculture, forestry and fisheries at the University of the South Pacific (USP) and Fiji National University (FNU). It is an Australian Government programme delivered by ACIAR, an Australian Government statutory authority, and is described by ACIAR as part of the Australian Government's support to Pacific neighbours. Scholarships are for Pacific Islander nationals and are awarded for up to two years at Master's level and up to three years for PhD candidates, with study available from Semester 1 2027.
new_scholarship.duration: Up to 2 years for Master's students; 3 years (or over, if applicable) for PhD candidates
new_scholarship.application_period: 2027 intake: applications open 20 August 2026 and close 21 October 2026, for scholarships available from Semester 1 2027. ACIAR states scholarships are advertised annually through USP and FNU for commencement the following year.
new_scholarship.eligibility_summary: Pacific Island country nationals who are citizens of and currently reside in Fiji, Kiribati, Samoa, Solomon Islands, Tonga, Tuvalu or Vanuatu (USP also lists the 12 USP member countries), who meet USP or FNU postgraduate entry requirements and can satisfy mandated travel requirements to Fiji or Samoa.
eligibility: Be a citizen of and currently reside in Fiji, Kiribati, Samoa, Solomon Islands, Tonga, Tuvalu or Vanuatu
Meet the eligibility criteria for postgraduate study at USP or FNU
Directly align the research proposal with a research topic in the PASS compendium, or develop a unique research proposal aligned with the compendium's broader research themes
Be able to meet government and university mandated requirements for travel to Fiji for study at FNU or USP Laucala, or to Samoa for study at USP Alafua

USP route: relevant Bachelor's degree with a GPA of 4.0 or above for Master's entry, or relevant Postgraduate Diploma plus Bachelor's with GPA 3.5 or over for both; or a relevant Bachelor's with GPA 4.5, a Master's by research, or a Master's with 25% or more independent research and a mini-thesis for PhD entry
USP route: 35 years or below when applying for Master's and 45 years or below for PhD, with flexibility considered in exceptional cases

Medical insurance at the prevailing rate
Books allowance, currently a one-off payment

programme_detail_official.description: The Pacific Agriculture Scholarships and Support (PASS) Program provides scholarships and support to postgraduate students in agriculture, forestry and fisheries at The University of the South Pacific (USP) and Fiji National University (FNU). Since 2005 ACIAR has supported research scholarships at Pacific universities as part of the Australian Government's support to its Pacific neighbours. Scholarships are offered in the Pacific to Pacific Islanders so that scholars can research agricultural problems in context, build relevant professional networks and remain close to family and culture.
programme_detail_official.coverage: Full tuition, living allowance, medical insurance, books allowance, relocation allowance and international conference funds for 24 months (Master's) or 3 years (PhD).

new_scholarship.name: John Allwright Fellowship
new_scholarship.official_source: Australian Centre for International Agricultural Research (ACIAR)
new_scholarship.description: The John Allwright Fellowship (JAF) is a competitive, merit-based postgraduate scholarship for scientists or economists from ACIAR partner countries who are currently or recently involved in ACIAR research projects. It funds Masters by Research or PhD study at an Australian tertiary institution and is administered through the Australia Awards system, with ACIAR providing additional pastoral care and professional development. The Fellowship is the largest investment in ACIAR's Capacity Development Program.
new_scholarship.deadline: Applications closed for the current round; the programme reopens annually
new_scholarship.application_period: Annual cycle. The ACIAR page showed 'Applications closed' on 2026-10-04; the next intake is expected to open in the same pattern as previous years, with applications historically opening early in the calendar year.
new_scholarship.eligibility_summary: Scientists or economists from ACIAR partner countries who are currently or recently involved in ACIAR research projects, seeking postgraduate qualifications at an Australian tertiary institution.
eligibility: Be a scientist or economist from an ACIAR partner country
Be currently or recently involved in an ACIAR research project
Seek admission to postgraduate study (Masters by Research or PhD) at an Australian tertiary institution
benefits: Masters by Research or PhD scholarship administered through the Australia Awards system
Pastoral care and development opportunities from ACIAR during the scholarship
requirements: Register an account in the Online Australia Scholarships Information System (OASIS)
Select the ACIAR John Allwright Fellowships award program when starting an application in OASIS
Sign a contract with the Commonwealth of Australia agreeing to comply with the conditions of the scholarship
application_method: Register an account in the Online Australia Scholarships Information System (OASIS)
Log on, create and complete an OASIS application form
Select the ACIAR John Allwright Fellowships award program
new_scholarship.selection_notes: ACIAR states the Fellowship is merit-based and that, in line with its gender equity commitment, women now comprise at least half of new Fellowship holders. The programme has also been allocating places in the 2026 intake round specifically for research on climate change, climate adaptation or strengthening resilience to climate change impacts.
new_scholarship.notes: Award holders are subject to a two-year post-study obligation: they must leave Australia for a minimum of two years after completing the scholarship, and failure to do so results in the scholar incurring a debt for the total accrued cost of the scholarship. An offer is only valid for the Australian academic year following the calendar year in which the offer is made.

programme_detail_official.description: The John Allwright Fellowship is a competitive, merit-based program available to scientists or economists from partner countries currently or recently involved in ACIAR research projects. It offers the opportunity to obtain formal postgraduate qualifications at an Australian tertiary institution. Its primary aim is to strengthen scientific research capability and institutional links in ACIAR partner countries to undertake high-quality and impactful research.
programme_detail_official.coverage: Not itemised on the ACIAR page read. The Fellowship is administered through the Australia Awards system and is subject to a bonded two-year obligation to leave Australia after completion.
